predecessors.name: Kimek-Kipchak confederation
predecessors.text: the steppe the Cumans came to hold in 1055 (Pontic-Caspian steppe outside the Kimek-Kipchak row's 1056 shape): not Kimek land; see the note

successors.name: Mongol Empire
successors.text: the Cuman steppe with the Bugeac, outside the Kimek-Kipchak row's 1072 shape (28-49 E), which the Cumans entered 'around 1068-1078'

ledger.x: 1055: the Cumans appear on the Pontic steppe at the Rus' frontier.

1072: Cliopatria's Kimek-Kipchak shape grows into 447 cells of this dossier's steppe (the Kimek dossier's 1072 gain of 'the southern Urals, Bashkortostan and the eastern and middle Volga') and keeps them to 1235.
1241: the Mongols end Cuman control of the steppe.

wars.name: Cuman wars with the Rus' princes
wars.outcome: In 1061 the Cumans under Sokal 'invaded and devastated the Pereyaslavl principality', which 'began a war that would go on for 175 years'; no frontier changed hands on the pages opened.

wars.name: Battle of the Alta River
wars.outcome: 'In 1068 at the Battle of the Alta River, the Cumans defeated the armies of the three sons of Yaroslav the Wise' (Iziaslav of Kiev, Sviatoslav of Chernigov, Vsevolod of Pereyaslavl).

wars.name: Cuman raids on Byzantium and Hungary
wars.outcome: Joint raid with the Pechenegs on Adrianople in 1078; Balkan raids from 1086; defeat by Ladislaus I of Hungary in 1089; the Pechenegs broken at Levounion in 1091 by Byzantines and Cumans; Paristrion 'conquered' in 1094-1095; Boniak crushes the Hungarian army…

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Cumania
wars.outcome: 'A direct attack on Cumania came only in 1238-1239'; large groups fled across the Danube in 1239-1240; 'The final blow came in 1241, when Cuman control over the Pontic steppes ended.'

certainty.note: A nomadic steppe confederation: neither page draws a frontier, and the extent of the steppe is the gazetteer's Pontic Steppe region minus the Kimek-Kipchak row (28-49 E).
